schema-upgrade.prompt: `openDb` is called with the path `":memory:"`. Which of these steps still runs?
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:221 sets `busy_timeout` for every path. src/db.ts:218 and src/db.ts:222-225 skip the folder, WAL and `synchronous` steps when the path is `":memory:"`.

schema-upgrade.prompt: The code calls `openDb("a.db")` and later calls `openDb("b.db")`. What happens to the connection to `a.db`?
options: It is reused, and `b.db` is not opened
It is closed before `b.db` is opened
`openDb` throws because a database is open
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:217 closes the stored `db` if there is one. Then src/db.ts:219 opens the new path and stores it in `db`.

schema-upgrade.prompt: A database is already open, and `dbGeneration` is 5. Code calls `resetSchema()` once. What is `dbGeneration` after the call?
schema-upgrade.explain: `db` is already set, so `getDb` on src/db.ts:235 does not call `openDb`. `resetSchema` calls `applySchema` once on src/db.ts:241, and src/db.ts:197 adds 1 to the counter.

schema-upgrade.prompt: Which of these invoice columns is not part of the index `invoices_workspace_search`?
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:152 lists workspace_id, issue_date, id, number, client_id, status and due_date. `notes` is not in the list.

schema-upgrade.prompt: Inside one workspace, in which order does the index `invoices_workspace_search` keep invoices?
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:152 lists `workspace_id`, then `issue_date DESC`, then `id DESC`, so after the workspace the rows go by newest date and then by highest id.

schema-upgrade.prompt: `resetSchema()` runs. What is the `foreign_keys` setting while the tables are dropped, and while `applySchema(d)` runs?
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:236 turns `foreign_keys` OFF before the DROP loop at src/db.ts:237-239, and src/db.ts:240 turns it ON again before `applySchema` at src/db.ts:241.

schema-upgrade.prompt: An old database has a column named `Notes` (capital N) in `invoices`. For the `ADDED_COLUMNS` entry with column `notes`, what does the check on line 193 decide?
options: It skips the entry and goes to the next table
It finds a match and skips ALTER TABLE
It finds no match and runs ALTER TABLE
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:193 compares names with `===`, which is case-sensitive. `"Notes" === "notes"` is false, so `some` returns false and ALTER TABLE runs.

schema-upgrade.prompt: A brand new, empty database is opened. How many times does `applySchema` run `PRAGMA table_info`?
options: 0, because the new table already has both columns
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:192 runs the PRAGMA inside the loop for every entry, before the check. `ADDED_COLUMNS` has two entries (src/db.ts:144-145), so it runs twice, even when no ALTER TABLE follows.

schema-upgrade.prompt: No database has been opened yet (`db` is `null`). Code calls `resetSchema()` once. How many times does `applySchema` run during this call?
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:235 calls `getDb()`, which calls `openDb()` because `db` is null (src/db.ts:231), and `openDb` runs `applySchema` at src/db.ts:226. Then src/db.ts:241 runs it a second time.

schema-upgrade.prompt: `applySchema` runs on any database. Which step runs directly before `dbGeneration++`?
schema-upgrade.explain: src/db.ts:195 runs `LATE_INDEXES`, then src/db.ts:196 runs `VERSION_SCHEMA`, and only then src/db.ts:197 increments `dbGeneration`.

search-filter-sql.prompt: How does a list row get its `line_count`?
options: From a COUNT subquery on line_items, run per invoice
From a counter column stored on the invoice
From JavaScript, after loading all line items
From a JOIN on line_items with GROUP BY
search-filter-sql.explain: Line 81 adds `(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM line_items li WHERE li.invoice_id = i.id) AS line_count` to the column list.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `s` is 99 letters `x`, then one space, then `yz` (102 characters in all). What does `parseSearch(s)` return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:27 collapses spaces and trims first, and only then cuts to `MAX_SEARCH` (100). The cut keeps the 99 `x` and the space, and nothing trims again after the cut.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `pageOf` is called with `total` = 0 and `pageNo` = 2. What does it return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:95 makes `pages` at least 1, even when there are no rows. src/lib/invoices.ts:96 then limits `page` to at most `pages`, so the result is 1.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `filterClause` is called with `workspaceId` = 7, `status` = `"overdue"`, `q` = `""` and `now` = `"2026-11-14"`. Which `params` does it return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:64-65 writes `'sent'` straight into the SQL text and pushes only `now`. The `else if` at line 66 is skipped, and with an empty `q` the call at line 70 adds no params.

search-filter-sql.prompt: A row has `status` `"sent"` and `due_date` `"2026-11-14"`. `now` is also `"2026-11-14"`. What do `inStatus(r, "overdue", now)` and `inStatus(r, "sent", now)` return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:85 uses a strict `<`, so a due date equal to today is not overdue. src/lib/invoices.ts:86 then matches `"sent"` directly.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `parseStatusFilter` is called with `"Paid"` (capital P). What does it return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:19 checks `includes` against the lowercase list from line 15. That check is case-sensitive, so `"Paid"` is not found and the function returns `"all"`.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `s` is a tab, then `Acme`, a space, a newline, two spaces, `Ltd`, and a space at the end. What does `parseSearch(s)` return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:27 turns every run of whitespace (tab, newline, spaces) into one space, which gives `" Acme Ltd "`. Then `trim` removes the space at each end.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `filterClause` is called with `workspaceId` = 3, `status` = `"paid"`, `q` = `"acme"` and some `now`. Which `params` does it return?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:62 starts with the workspace id and line 68 adds `"paid"`. Line 71 then adds the search params last, and those are the `%acme%` pattern built at line 76, once for each column.

search-filter-sql.prompt: `listInvoices(1, "all", 1, " ")` is called. The search text is one space. Which function runs?
options: Neither, it returns an empty result
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:91 only checks whether `q` is truthy. It does not trim, and a one-space string is truthy, so `searchInvoices` runs.

search-filter-sql.prompt: A workspace has 2 draft invoices, 3 sent invoices (one of them has a `due_date` before today) and 1 paid invoice. Which values does `browseInvoices` put in `counts`?
search-filter-sql.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:106 counts all 6 rows. Line 108 counts every sent row (3), and line 109 counts the sent row that is past due (1) in a separate column, so that row is counted in both sent and overdue.

searched-list.prompt: A search matches 4 invoices. All 4 have status `"sent"`, and 3 of them have a `due_date` before `now`. The user is on the Sent tab. What is `total`?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:157-159 add one to `counts.sent` for every sent invoice, and also add to `counts.overdue` when it is past due. So `counts.sent` is 4, and src/lib/invoices.ts:162 sets `total` to `counts["sent"]`.

searched-list.prompt: A matching invoice has status `"sent"` and its `due_date` is the same string as `now` (today). Which counts does this invoice add 1 to?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:153 starts `all` at the length of `matches`, which includes this invoice. src/lib/invoices.ts:158 adds to `sent`, and src/lib/invoices.ts:159 adds to `overdue` only when `due_date < now`, which is false for an equal date.

searched-list.prompt: A matching invoice has status `"cancelled"`. Which counts include it?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:153 sets `all` to `matches.length`, so every match is in it. The checks at src/lib/invoices.ts:155-157 only match `"draft"`, `"paid"` and `"sent"`, so no other count goes up.

searched-list.prompt: `PAGE_SIZE` is 20 and `pageOf` returns `page` 2. Which items of `inTab` (counted from 0) give the ids for the page?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:165 calls `inTab.slice((2 - 1) * 20, 2 * 20)`, which is `slice(20, 40)`. That takes items 20 to 39.

searched-list.prompt: A matching invoice has status `"draft"`, and its `due_date` is last month, so it is before `now`. Which counts does this invoice add 1 to?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:153 sets `all` to the full length, and src/lib/invoices.ts:155 adds to `draft`. The due date check at src/lib/invoices.ts:159 runs only inside the `"sent"` branch.

searched-list.prompt: Two matching invoices have the same `issue_date`. One has id 7 and the other has id 9. Which one comes first in `matches`?
options: The one with the earlier due date
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:149 orders by `issue_date DESC, id DESC`, so when the dates are equal the higher id comes first.

searched-list.prompt: The user is on the Overdue tab. The search matches 4 invoices: 2 `"sent"` with `due_date` before `now`, 1 `"sent"` with `due_date` after `now`, and 1 `"draft"`. What is `total`?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:159 adds to `overdue` only for sent invoices with a due date before `now`, which gives 2. src/lib/invoices.ts:162 sets `total` to `counts[status]`.

searched-list.prompt: The user is on the Paid tab. The search matches 6 invoices, and none of them is paid, so `inTab` is empty. What happens to `rows`?
options: It is `null`, and no third query runs
It is `[]`, and no third query runs
It is `[]`, after a third query finds nothing
searched-list.explain: With an empty `inTab`, src/lib/invoices.ts:165 gives an empty `ids`. src/lib/invoices.ts:166 then picks the `[]` branch on line 176 and does not run the query.

searched-list.prompt: The user is on the All tab. The search matches 3 invoices: 2 `"draft"` and 1 `"cancelled"`. `PAGE_SIZE` is 20 and `pageOf` returns `page` 1. How many ids are in `ids`?
searched-list.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:164 uses `matches` with no filter when `status` is `"all"`, so the cancelled invoice stays in. src/lib/invoices.ts:165 then takes items 0 to 19, which is all 3.

list-page.explain: Lines 48 to 50 set `q` first, then `status`, and add `page` only when it is greater than 1. Line 74 builds every tab link with page 1.

list-page.prompt: The user is on the Overdue tab and submits the search form with new text. How does the next request know the status?
options: The form action has `?status=overdue` in it
It does not, the list returns to the All tab
A hidden `status` input is part of the form
The status is read from the session
list-page.explain: Line 108 adds a hidden input named `status` when the current status is not `all`, so the form sends it together with `q`.

list-page.prompt: The user is on the Overdue tab (`status` is `"overdue"`) and searches for `q = "acme"`. No invoices match. Where does the "Clear search" link in the empty table message point?
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:79 builds the link with `listHref(status, "", 1)`. The empty `q` and page 1 are left out, but the status stays (src/routes/invoices.ts:48-50).

list-page.prompt: A search is active: `status` is `"paid"` and `q` is `"acme"`. Which value does the page header show as the number before "matching"?
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:118 prints `res.counts.all` when `q` is set. It does not use the count for the current tab or the page rows.

list-page.prompt: A search finds nothing, so `res.total` is `0` and `res.page` is `1`. What text does the pager show before the page buttons?
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:96 sets `from` to 0 when the total is 0, and src/routes/invoices.ts:97 takes the smaller of `page * PAGE_SIZE` and 0, which is 0.

list-page.prompt: A row has `number` `"INV-7"` and `line_count` `0`. What does the small screen line under the client name show?
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:86 uses "item" only when `line_count === 1`. For 0 it prints the number and "items".

list-page.prompt: `status` is `"all"` and `q` is `""`. Which elements does the search form render, besides the search box and the Search button?
options: A Clear link and the Export CSV link
A hidden status input and the Export CSV link
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:108 adds the hidden input only when status is not "all". src/routes/invoices.ts:111 adds Clear only when `q` is not empty. src/routes/invoices.ts:112 always adds the Export CSV link.

list-page.prompt: `status` is `"all"`, `q` is `""`, and the list has no rows. What text is shown in the empty table cell?
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:77 adds no label when status is "all", so `what` is "invoices". `q` is empty, so src/routes/invoices.ts:80 is used: "No invoices."

list-page.prompt: `status` is `"paid"`, `q` is `""`, and `res.page` is `2`. Where does the Previous link point?
list-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:101 calls `listHref(status, q, res.page - 1)`, which is page 1. `listQuery` (src/routes/invoices.ts:48-50) skips the empty `q` and skips page 1, but keeps `status=paid`.

list-page.prompt: A row has `client_id` `4` and `client_name` `"Acme"`. How does the JSON from `GET /invoices` in the API show the client?
list-page.explain: src/routes/api.ts:51 puts both values in one nested `client` object with the keys `id` and `name`.

src/routes/invoices.ts:47-48 put `q` into a `URLSearchParams`. Its `toString()` at src/routes/invoices.ts:51 encodes a space as `+` and `&` as `%26`. Status "all" and page 1 are left out (lines 49-50).

notes.prompt: A JSON body for a new invoice has `"notes": 42`. What is stored in the `notes` column?
notes.explain: Line 229 returns an empty string for any value that is not a string. `createInvoice` then stores that string.

notes.prompt: A JSON body for a new invoice has no `notes` key. `createInvoice` is called with `status` "draft". What goes into the `notes` column?
options: The column default, whatever it is
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:262 sets `notes` to `null` when the key is missing. Line 341 passes `input.notes ?? ""`, so an empty string is inserted.

notes.prompt: A JSON body has `items: [{ "description": "Design", "quantity": 2 }]` with no `unit_price`. What is `unit_price` of that item after `readInvoiceForm`?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:241 takes the array branch, and line 245 does `String(it?.unit_price ?? "")`. The missing value becomes "", so the result is an empty string.

notes.prompt: A form body has `description` = `"A"` and also `description[]` = `["B", "C"]`. It has no quantity or unit price fields. How many items does `readInvoiceForm` return?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:248 uses `??`, so `body["description"]` ("A") wins and `asList` makes it a list of one. Lines 249-251 give empty lists for the others, so `n` is 1.

notes.prompt: A user calls `GET /invoices/:id` with the id of an invoice that exists but belongs to another workspace. What does the API return?
notes.explain: src/routes/api.ts:74-75 finds the invoice, so there is no 404. Line 76 then sees a different `workspace_id` and returns 403 with `forbidden`.

notes.prompt: A JSON body has an `items` list with `MAX_LINES + 5` entries. How many items does `readInvoiceForm` return?
options: 0, because the list is too long
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:242 keeps `slice(0, MAX_LINES + 1)` of the list, so one item more than `MAX_LINES` is kept.

notes.prompt: A JSON body has `items: [{ "description": "Fix", "quantity": 0, "unit_price": "5" }]`. What is `quantity` of that item after `readInvoiceForm`?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:244 uses `??`, which only replaces `null` or `undefined`. So 0 is kept and `String(0)` gives "0".

notes.prompt: A form body has `description[]` = `["A", "B", "C"]`, `quantity` = `"1"`, and no unit price field. There is no `items` key. Assume `MAX_LINES` is more than 3. How many items does `readInvoiceForm` return?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:248-250 give lists of length 3, 1 and 0. Line 251 takes the largest length, 3, and line 253 loops that many times.

notes.prompt: A JSON body has `items: []` and also a top-level `description` of `"A"`. How many items does `readInvoiceForm` return?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:241 checks only that `body.items` is an array. An empty array is one, so line 242 maps it to an empty list and the `description` field is never read.

notes.prompt: An invoice has the stored notes "Pay by card". `updateInvoice` is called with `input.notes` set to `""`. What are the stored notes after the call?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:358 calls `setNotes` whenever `notes` is not `null`, and "" is not `null`. Line 364 then writes "" to the column.

notes.prompt: `blankForm(30)` is called for a new invoice. What is in `items` of the result?
notes.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:315 returns one item with an empty description, `quantity` "1" and an empty unit price.

share-token.prompt: A signed-in user from another workspace posts to `/invoices/:id/share/revoke`. What happens?
options: A 404 page, as if the invoice did not exist
A redirect to the invoice list
A 403 page, and the token is unchanged
share-token.explain: Lines 368 to 370 return a 403 page when the invoice belongs to another workspace. The route returns that error before it reaches `revokeShare`.

share-token.prompt: The owner of invoice 7 posts to `/invoices/7/share/revoke` and the check in `ownInvoice` passes. Where does the response redirect to?
share-token.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:385 redirects to the invoice page with `done=unshared` and the `#share` anchor. src/routes/invoices.ts:43 has the matching `unshared` message.

share-token.prompt: Some code calls `enableShare(999)` directly, and no invoice has `id` 999. What happens?
options: It throws an error when it reads `share_token`
It inserts a new row with the token
It returns the new random token
share-token.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:375 updates no row. src/lib/invoices.ts:376 then gets no row from the SELECT, and the `!` only affects the type check. So reading `.share_token` on the missing row throws.

share-token.prompt: A page has a button with `data-copy="#missing"`, and no element on the page matches `#missing`. The user clicks the button. What happens?
options: The script stops, and nothing is selected or copied
An empty string is copied and the label shows `Copied`
The whole page text is selected and copied
The script throws an error because `input` is null
share-token.explain: public/app.js:49 gets `null` from `querySelector`, and public/app.js:50 returns before `input.select()` or any copy runs.

share-token.prompt: Invoice 7 has a `share_token`. The owner opens `/invoices/7`. What text does the badge in the head of the share card show?
share-token.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:311 picks the first card when a token exists, and src/routes/invoices.ts:313 puts a `badge-sent` span with the text `Active` in its head.

share-token.prompt: Invoice 7 has `share_token` set to `NULL`. The owner opens `/invoices/7`. What is the value of `shareUrl`?
share-token.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:310 builds the URL only when `invoice.share_token` is truthy. Otherwise it uses `""`.

share-token.prompt: The Copy button has a small `<span>` icon inside it. The user clicks exactly on the icon, so `e.target` is the span. What does the script do?
options: It copies the input, as for a click on the button
It copies the text of the span
It throws, because the span has no `data-copy`
Nothing, because the target is not a button
share-token.explain: public/app.js:47 uses `closest("button[data-copy]")`, which walks up from the span to the button. Lines 49-51 then find and select the input.

share-token.prompt: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` exists and its promise resolves. The user clicks Copy. What does the button label show 3 seconds after the copy finished?
share-token.explain: public/app.js:53 sets the label to `Copied`, and public/app.js:54 sets it back to `Copy` after 2000 ms.

share-token.prompt: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` exists, but its promise is rejected. The user clicks Copy on the share card. Is the text in the `#share-url` input selected afterwards?
options: No, the script never selects the text
No, the text is selected only after a successful write
Yes, the text is selected before the write is tried
No, the selection is cleared when the write fails
share-token.explain: public/app.js:51 calls `input.select()` before any copy is tried, and the reject handler on public/app.js:57 is an empty function that does not undo it.

public-page.prompt: A line item has `quantity` 0.5 and `unit_price` 125. Which number does `invoicePaper` pass to `money` for the Amount cell of this row?
public-page.explain: src/views/invoice.ts:13 computes `Math.round(li.quantity * li.unit_price)`. That is `Math.round(62.5)`, which gives 63 in JavaScript.

public-page.prompt: The workspace has `iban` set. The invoice has `number` "INV-12" and `reference` "PO-77". Which reference does the "Pay to" line show?
public-page.explain: src/views/invoice.ts:49 writes `reference ${esc(invoice.number)}`. It uses the invoice number, not `invoice.reference`.

public-page.prompt: The workspace has `legal_name` set to an empty string and `name` set to "Acme". What text does the "from" block at the top of the document show?
public-page.explain: src/views/invoice.ts:21 uses `ws.legal_name || ws.name`. An empty string is falsy, so the code uses `name`, which is "Acme".

public-page.prompt: Someone opens `/share/abc`, and no invoice has the token "abc". Does the 404 response have the `X-Robots-Tag` header?
options: No, the header is only set on success
public-page.explain: src/routes/share.ts:13 sets the header before the lookup on line 14. The 404 return on line 16 comes after that, so the header is already set.

public-page.prompt: Someone opens a valid share link for the invoice with `number` "INV-12". Which title does the share route pass to `bare`?
public-page.explain: src/routes/share.ts:27 calls `bare` with the template `Invoice ${invoice.number}`, which gives "Invoice INV-12".

public-page.prompt: On the share page, the workspace has `legal_name` "Acme Ltd", `name` "Acme" and `email` set to an empty string. What text does the small line in the share header show?
public-page.explain: src/routes/share.ts:23 uses `ws.legal_name || ws.name`, which is "Acme Ltd". The email part is added only when `ws.email` is not empty, so nothing follows the name.

public-page.prompt: The client has `contact_name` "" and `vat_id` "DE9". The workspace has `vat_id` "". What appears under the client name in the "Billed to" block?
options: The contact, the address, then "VAT DE9"
public-page.explain: src/views/invoice.ts:32 skips the contact because `contact_name` is empty. Line 33 always shows the address, and line 34 then shows the client VAT because `client.vat_id` is set.

public-page.prompt: `invoicePaper` gets two items whose Amount cells add up to 100, and `total` is 120. Which number does the Total cell pass to `money`?
options: 0, because the values do not match
public-page.explain: src/views/invoice.ts:46 writes `money(total)`. It uses the `total` value given to the function and does not add up the rows.

public-page.prompt: On the owner's invoice page, what does the small line under the heading show?
public-page.explain: src/routes/invoices.ts:350 writes the client name, then `money(total)`, then "due" and the formatted `due_date`.

csv-export.prompt: An invoice's notes are `-5, thanks`. Which text does `csvField` return?
csv-export.explain: Line 11 puts an apostrophe in front because the text starts with `-`. Line 12 then wraps the result in double quotes because it holds a comma.

csv-export.prompt: A client name is the text ` =A1`: one space, then `=A1`. Which text does `csvField` return for it?
csv-export.explain: src/lib/csv.ts:11 adds the apostrophe only when the first character is one of = + - @ tab CR. Here the first character is a space, so nothing is added. src/lib/csv.ts:12 finds no quote, comma or line break, so the text comes back unchanged.

csv-export.prompt: One invoice matches the filter but has no line items. What does `exportInvoices` return for it?
options: No row, because the join finds no line items
A row with `total` and `line_count` set to null
csv-export.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:196 uses a LEFT JOIN, so the invoice is kept even when the subquery has no row for it. src/lib/invoices.ts:193 turns the missing values into 0 with COALESCE.

csv-export.prompt: Workspace 9 has no row in `workspace_versions`. A client is inserted in workspace 9. Then the name of that client is updated. What does `workspaceVersion(9)` return after this?
csv-export.explain: src/db.ts:169 inserts the row with version 1 on the first write. src/db.ts:170 adds 1 on the next write. The clients trigger at src/db.ts:177-178 raises the counter once per write, even for an update, so the result is 2.

csv-export.prompt: Three invoices match the filter. Invoice 3 has `issue_date` `2026-04-01`. Invoices 5 and 8 both have `issue_date` `2026-03-01`. In which order does `exportInvoices` return them?
csv-export.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:203 sorts by `issue_date` from newest to oldest, so invoice 3 comes first. Invoices 5 and 8 have the same date, so they are sorted by `id` from high to low, which puts 8 before 5.

csv-export.prompt: An invoice matches the filter, but its `client_id` is 7 and no row in `clients` has id 7. What does `exportInvoices` return for this invoice?
options: A row with `client_name` set to an empty text
csv-export.explain: src/lib/invoices.ts:195 uses a plain `JOIN` on clients, not a `LEFT JOIN`. An invoice with no matching client is dropped from the result.
